acceptedAnswer.text: For standard adult screening, a BMI from 18.5 to 24.9 is commonly classified as healthy weight. This range is not a guarantee of health and does not replace an individual assessment.
No. BMI is a useful population and screening measure, but it cannot distinguish muscle from fat or show where fat is stored. It should be interpreted with other relevant health information.

mainEntity.name: Can I use this BMI calculator for children?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. This page uses adult BMI categories. Children and teenagers need BMI-for-age assessment using age- and sex-specific growth references.

mainEntity.name: Does BMI diagnose obesity or another disease?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. BMI is a screening measure. A healthcare professional can consider BMI together with medical history, physical findings, health behaviours and other relevant measurements.

mainEntity.name: How is the healthy-weight range calculated?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a given height, the calculator applies the standard adult BMI range of 18.5 to 24.9 to estimate the corresponding weight range. It is an estimate based on BMI, not a personalized target weight.

mainEntity.name: Why are there lower BMI cut-offs for Asian populations?

acceptedAnswer.text: A 2004 WHO expert consultation found that many Asian populations have more body fat and a higher risk of type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease at a given BMI than European populations. It kept the international categories but proposed public-health action points of 23 (increased risk) and 27.5 (high risk).
BMI Prime is your BMI divided by 25, the upper limit of the healthy range. A value below 1.0 is under the overweight threshold; for example, 1.2 means your BMI is 20% above it.

mainEntity.name: What is the New Oxford BMI?

acceptedAnswer.text: It's an alternative formula, 1.3 × weight (kg) ÷ height (m) to the power 2.5, proposed by Oxford mathematician Nick Trefethen. It reduces the way standard BMI makes tall people look heavier and short people look lighter, but it is not used for official clinical categories.
